title: What should I ask and check when I visit a sales gallery?
videoTitle: The Science behind Show Units | Vlog 003
excerpt: Show units are built to stir your emotions. Sean lists the questions to ask a sales team, what to check in a show unit, and why floor premiums make top floors hard to sell.

qa.context: The big developers have refined the arrival at a sales gallery, from the landscaped drive to the guard who opens the door and the staff who brief you, and they spend heavily on show units.
qa.question: How should a buyer approach a sales gallery and show unit?
qa.answer: Go to listen and to ask, and keep a realistic mind: the actual unit won't look like the show unit. Check what is really included, take package offers away to think about, and keep visiting other projects so you aren't swept along by one pitch.

reasons.title: Questions reveal the value
reasons.body: Ask the current sales status, why people are buying, what is special about the location, what will be built next, and how the developer will protect buyers' interests.

reasons.title: Show units aren't always the spec
reasons.body: Developers sometimes change the flooring, walls or sanitary fittings in a show unit to make it look its best. Check which finishes you will actually get.

reasons.title: Floor premiums add up
reasons.body: Prices often rise by RM1,000 or RM2,000 for every floor, which is why many projects struggle to sell their highest, most expensive floors.

actions: Prepare your questions on sales status, location and future plans before you go.
Ask which flooring, walls and fittings are included, and get it in writing.
Take any package offer away and think it over.
Visit a project on Saturday and another on Sunday to broaden your comparison.
Use show units for ideas for your own home, not as a promise.
qa.caveat: Some offers are genuinely good, and Sean warns against overthinking: if you never buy, prices may only be higher years later.

sourceNote: Summarised from Sean's English captions for this November 2017 vlog, filmed at a developer's sales gallery where a salesperson he knows hosted him; he says he was not paid. The quoted line is verbatim; everything else is paraphrased. His explanation of price per square foot is covered in a separate guide.
